scenario: At most one fault is pending per (node, rule) site between a raise and the drain (LERR.9.7): a later fault at a site still pending replaces it, and the stream carries the drained fact only. Drives ONE propagation that faults twice at ONE site with two kinds: the join test of rule `ratio`'s beta on Q (a two-pattern `where`, so a join test, IRET.6.4) is evaluated against both Q facts when P arrives. Q `zero` traps DIVIDE_BY_ZERO on the Int `//`; Q `huge` traps NOT_REPRESENTABLE in `floor` of 1e300. Both are ComputationErrors at the same beta under the matching-time name `$beta_<id>` (LERR.9.11), so their fault facts differ in `kind` alone. Without coalescing the drain asserts the first, then supersedes it with the second (LERR.9.5), and the stream carries a `fact_retract` for the first; with it there is one pending fault and one assertion, and nothing retracts, whichever candidate the beta evaluates last. Nothing else in the scenario retracts: every fact has a fresh key. LERR.9.7_one_pending_per_site_fires pins that the faults are raised and their fact asserted, so this vector cannot pass by raising nothing. Pin: assert Q(zero), Q(huge), P; pump. No `fact_retract`.
rules_ds:
from math import floor

schema P scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    n: Int mutable

schema Q scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    d: Int mutable
    f: Float mutable

rule ratio:
    P p
    Q q where (p.n // q.d) > floor(q.f)
->
    log info "ratio"
